clue.text: Naive Parisian I spotted with girl of the month

parts.note: a Parisian says je for I in French
June is a girl's name that is also the name of a month

explanation.surface: A naive Frenchman is seen out with a girl, the calendar's pin-up of the month.
explanation.definitionFit: Jejune describes ideas or people that are simplistic and unsophisticated, a synonym of naive.

clue.text: Girl gives Jack ponies he ordered

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards

indicators.note: the letters of ponies and he are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A girl receives ponies that her friend Jack ordered for her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' is the card abbreviation; 'ordered' is the anagram signal, so the ponies are rearranged with 'he', not bought.
explanation.definitionFit: Josephine is a woman's given name, so it is an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: Moor finally became 50 green

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's Moor, Othello, ends up consumed by suspicion of his wife
envy and suspicion are proverbially green, the green-eyed monster

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's Moor ended the play green with suspicion.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is the archetype of the envious husband, and green is the colour of envy, as in the green-eyed monster.

clue.text: Book about the French never counted

indicators.note: the book's name goes round the other piece, standing about it

parts.note: Numbers is the fourth book of the Old Testament
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: A book on the French people that has never been counted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something countless or innumerable cannot be or has never been numbered.

clue.text: Fashionable people in trial beaks put back

indicators.note: the two words are put back to front, the whole run read in reverse

parts.note: a test is a trial
a ram is the beak of a warship, used to strike other ships

explanation.surface: Fashionable people at a trial see the magistrates put back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaks' suggests British magistrates; here they are ships' rams. 'put back' reverses TESTRAMS as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The smart set is the fashionable, sophisticated social elite.

clue.text: Part of 11 that's 15

parts.note: the borough of the city at 11 across that is an island, and so is insular (15 across)

explanation.surface: A cross-reference clue: a part of the city at 11 that is the word at 15.
explanation.definitionFit: This borough of the great American city stands on an island, so it is literally island-bound, the sense of the word at 15.

clue.text: Moves boats from banks

definitions.meaning: tiers or lines, as in banks of seats or oars

explanation.surface: Someone pushes boats away from the riverbanks.
explanation.definitionFit: To propel a boat with oars is to row, and banks of seats are tiers, which are lines.

clue.text: Made speech about an American city

indicators.note: the verb's letters go round the next piece, standing about it

parts.note: spoke means made speech

explanation.surface: Someone gave a speech about an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Spokane is a city in Washington State in the north-western United States.

clue.text: Wine acceptable after tea, say

indicators.note: the first piece comes after the second, so tea's letter leads

parts.note: tea is pronounced like the letter T, as signalled by say
okay means acceptable

explanation.surface: A wine that is quite acceptable after afternoon tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokay is a sweet dessert wine from the Tokaj region of Hungary.

clue.text: Sign to move 29

definitions.meaning: a sign of the zodiac, Cancer
to scuttle in the manner of the clue at 29, obliquely

explanation.surface: A cross-reference clue: a sign to shift in the direction of 29.
explanation.definitionFit: Cancer's zodiac symbol is the shellfish, and as a verb the word means to move sideways like one.

clue.text: Not a genuine performer in second field event

parts.note: the hammer throw is an athletics field event

explanation.surface: An athlete who fakes it competes in the second field event.
explanation.definitionFit: A shammer is someone who feigns or pretends, a performer whose act is fake.

clue.text: Queens may be found in this modern royal house

definitions.text: Queens may be found in this

parts.note: new means modern
the House of York was an English royal dynasty

explanation.surface: Queens are to be found in this modern royal dynasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queens' looks like female monarchs; it is the borough of the American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Queens is one of the five boroughs of this American city.

clue.text: Notorious April disaster, trapping more than 20

annotationWithheld.clue: Notorious April disaster, trapping more than 20

clue.text: Nursery gardener or shepherdess

definitions.meaning: the quite contrary nursery-rhyme girl whose garden grows silver bells
the nursery-rhyme girl who had a little lamb

explanation.surface: A nursery rhyme gardener, or perhaps a shepherdess.
explanation.definitionFit: Two nursery rhymes share this girl's name: one tends a garden of cockle shells, the other keeps a little lamb.

clue.text: One composer has game of cards with another

parts.note: monte is a gambling card game, as in three-card monte
Verdi is another composer, the Italian opera writer

explanation.surface: One composer plays a card game with another.
explanation.definitionFit: Claudio Monteverdi was an Italian composer of early opera and madrigals.

clue.text: Some keys are so narrow

definitions.meaning: keys are low islands, as in the Florida Keys, and so belong to an island

explanation.surface: Some piano keys are so narrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Insular means of an island, and figuratively narrow-minded or parochial.

clue.text: Service with which Albert was initially associated

definitions.text: Service with which Albert was initially associated

parts.words: Service with which Albert was initially associated
parts.note: Prince Albert, later King George VI, began his career as a naval cadet and officer in Britain's sea-going armed service

explanation.surface: Asks which service Albert was first connected with.
explanation.definitionFit: The future George VI, known as Albert, served at sea in Britain's naval service and fought at Jutland.

clue.text: Plant row elsewhere, using these?

indicators.note: the answer uses letters running through the words before it

explanation.surface: To move a row of plants somewhere else, you might use these garden tools.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run consecutively through 'planT ROW ELSewhere', and the whole clue describes the garden tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Trowels are small hand tools used for digging up and replanting.

clue.text: Virginia's husband, perhaps, is a politician

definitions.meaning: Virginia is a US state, so her man could be called the ...

explanation.surface: Virginia's husband might be a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A statesman is an experienced, respected political leader; jokingly, a man belonging to a state such as Virginia.

clue.text: My bases involved in mission

indicators.note: the letters of my bases are tangled together, involved with one another

explanation.surface: My military bases are involved in a mission.
explanation.definitionFit: A mission is a diplomatic delegation abroad, and an embassy is the same thing or its building.

clue.text: Conceited fellow makes important point

parts.note: big means important
a head is a point, as of a spear or promontory

explanation.surface: A conceited person makes an important point.
explanation.definitionFit: A bighead is a boastful, arrogant person full of self-importance.

clue.text: Ah! Tempter repelled her

indicators.note: pushed back, so the run of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: Satan, the Tempter of Christ in the wilderness

explanation.surface: Ah, she repelled the tempter who tried to lead her astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repelled' turns AHSATAN round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Natasha is a woman's given name, so it is an example of a female person.

clue.text: Stone fish

definitions.meaning: a ... stone is a red gemstone, sardius
a small oily fish of the herring family

explanation.surface: A fish turned to stone.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the gem sardius, mentioned in the Bible, and a small tinned fish like a pilchard.

clue.text: Imprison with four keys

parts.note: C is a musical key
A is a musical key
G is a musical key
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Lock someone up with four keys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keys' suggests locks; here they are musical keys, each a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To cage someone is to shut them in behind bars, to imprison them.

clue.text: What's many a fool? That's about right

definitions.text: What's many a fool? That's about right

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Is many a fool stupid? That's about right.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and C (about) and R (right) followed by ASS (fool) build the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Crass means grossly stupid or insensitive, which describes many a fool.

clue.text: Ken's verbal composition, poetry of a sort

indicators.note: the letters are composed into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: Ken's supplies its letters with the s

explanation.surface: Ken has composed some verbal work, a kind of poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrhymed iambic pentameter, as used by Shakespeare and Milton, is a form of poetry.

clue.text: Handle dropped in attempt to impress

definitions.text: Handle dropped in attempt to impress

parts.words: Handle dropped in attempt to impress
parts.note: a handle is slang for a person's label, and dropping a famous one into conversation is a way of showing off

explanation.surface: A door handle drops off while someone tries to make an impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Handle is slang for what someone is called, and name-dropping is mentioning celebrities to impress.

clue.text: Consider prospect

explanation.surface: Weigh up a prospect.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to consider it, and a scenic outlook is a prospect.

clue.text: Little by little, otherwise, in a mother country

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other two

parts.note: ma is mother
Eric, or, Little by Little is a Victorian school novel by F. W. Farrar, so its other title is Eric

explanation.surface: Little by little, things change in a motherland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little by little' looks like a phrase meaning gradually; it is the subtitle of the novel Eric, a Victorian British school story.
explanation.definitionFit: America is a familiar name for the United States, a nation.

clue.text: M6 sign reversed — for those on the left

definitions.note: a doctrine, not people: the creed meant for left-wingers

indicators.note: the whole run of letters is turned round

parts.note: six is the number 6
the Ram, Aries, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A road sign on the M6 motorway is turned round, for drivers on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'M6' looks like the British motorway; it is M plus SIX. 'reversed' turns MSIXRAM as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The socialist doctrine of Karl Marx is the classic creed of left-wing politics.

clue.text: Oblique team movements

parts.note: a side is a team
ways are movements, as when a ship gathers way

explanation.surface: A team's oblique movements on the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving sideways means slanting or moving at an angle, which is oblique.

clue.text: Tribesman in some trouble

indicators.note: the letters of in some are troubled into disorder

explanation.surface: A member of a tribe finds himself in some trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Simeon was a son of Jacob and founder of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
